newsitem.title: USA: New York to drop charges against Danish mother.
newsitem.headline: New York to drop charges against Danish mother.

text.p: Authorities were expected to drop charges on Friday against a Danish woman arrested for leaving her baby outside a New York restaurant in an apparent clash of cultures, legal sources close to the case said.
The sources said that in a deal with prosecutors, Danish actress Annette Sorensen had agreed to leave the United States and fly home to Denmark at the weekend.

Sorensen's 14-month-old baby Liv was put in foster care for four days following the mother's arrest on Saturday night on charges of endangering the welfare of a child. Sorensen spent two days in jail before being reunited with her child on Wednesday night.
Sorensen, 30, who had been scheduled to appear in Manhattan Criminal Court on Monday, was expected at a hearing later on Friday afternoon when the case would be closed, the legal sources said.

The mother's attorneys said Sorensen did not think twice about leaving the child in a stroller outside the East Village restaurant because it was common practice in Copenhagen, but officials questioned the wisdom of being so trusting in New York.

Authorities took the 14-month-old baby from her mother and American father, Exavier Wardlaw, on Saturday. The couple had left her outside the restaurant while they were inside having a drink and watching her through the window, police said.
Passers-by who said the baby was cold and crying called police, they said.
An attorney for the father said Sorensen had been in the United States less than 48 hours when her daughter was taken from her.
